newsitem.title: GERMANY: PowerGen has no plans to bid for Bewag.
newsitem.headline: PowerGen has no plans to bid for Bewag.

text.p: British power group PowerGen Plc, one of three possible foreign bidders for German state utility group Berliner Kraft- und Licht AG (BEWAG), said on Wednesday it was not planning to make a bid for the group.

"We looked very closely at the commercial opportunities presented by the Bewag sale, however we have decided not to make a bid. And in the current circumstances it is unlikely that we will pursue our interest further in Bewag," PowerGen press officer Mike Pollak told Reuters by telephone.
PowerGen says has no plans to make bid for =2

The Berlin government had earlier said it may be forced to reopen the bidding in the Bewag privatisation if all foreign companies on the short-list of potential bidders dropped out of the running. But it also said that talks were continuing with all companies.

Industry sources had said a consortium of two German bidders, Veba AG and VIAG AG's units PreussenElektra and Bayernwerk, as well as U.S. groups Enron and Southern Company and U.K. group PowerGen were still in the running early this week.
Pollak declined to be more specific about why PowerGen dropped out of the bidding and when it reached its decision.
Pollak added PowerGen remained generally interested in the German utility market, particularly as it is already involved in Mibrag Mining and Schkopau Power Station.
